findings.title: WebCrypto Ed25519 availability is an external runtime fact, mitigated but not pre-proven
findings.problem: Workers runtime support for crypto.subtle Ed25519 is asserted as 'expected'; only HMAC/PBKDF2 are proven in-repo (verified crypto.ts). Design proceeds on an unverified primitive-availability assumption until the implementation smoke test runs.
findings.fix: Keep the §10.1 importKey/sign/verify Ed25519 smoke test as the FIRST finalize-e2e step; gate WebCrypto-vs-@noble on its pasted result and record the outcome in memory/decisions.md (SL-1).

findings.title: AC-2 'exactly twelve fields' depends on a design-asserted edit to the requirements doc
findings.problem: Design claims it edited requirements FR-2/AC-2 to include activation_allowed. The requirements file read does list all twelve fields, so they agree now, but doc-mutates-doc coupling can drift silently if either is regenerated.
findings.fix: Add a conformance test asserting the signed payload key set equals the AC-2 enumerated set from one shared constant, so neither doc nor code can drift without a red test.

findings.title: issued_at == server_time duplication carried without a current consumer
findings.problem: issued_at and server_time are specified as always equal 'by construction', kept only for a hypothetical future protocol version. Two identical signed fields with no divergence rule in v1.
findings.fix: In CLIENT_INTEGRATION.md require the v1 client to reject payloads where issued_at != server_time (turning the redundancy into a free tamper check), or state the client ignores issued_at in v1. Prefer the former.

findings.title: Freshness predicate accepts in-window replays and the max-age ceiling is a server-controlled soft knob
findings.problem: Replay defense is server_time monotonicity + max-age of verification_interval_seconds + 300s SKEW; a still-in-window replay is accepted (meets AC-28/OQ-8). A misconfigured large server interval widens the replay window silently.
findings.fix: Document a hard client-side ceiling, e.g. min(verification_interval_seconds, 86400) + SKEW, in CLIENT_INTEGRATION.md and the checker; carry the server-issued nonce as the OQ-8 follow-up.

findings.title: Shared app_secret in checker/desktop is an auto-hold DoS surface; default correct, document residual risk at contract level
findings.problem: /verify and /report authenticate with a shared app_secret, so any holder can report. Auto-hold correctly defaults to corroboration (N>=2 distinct installation_hash, single-report-immediate-hold OFF) and routes the real fix via OQ-1 ASK-FIRST. Reasonable Phase-1 posture, not a defect.
findings.fix: In CLIENT_INTEGRATION.md state app_secret is a shared app credential (not per-device identity) and /report is advisory/corroboration-gated; carry OQ-1 device-token alternative as the documented path if the desktop threat model later forbids shipping app_secret. No Phase-1 code change.
